headline: High risk of cascading error and data leakage: LightAgent can ingest Airflow outputs via MCP/stdio while both have broad egress, creating unsafe default handoff paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can emit task outputs and LightAgent can consume tool/input streams via MCP/stdio, so a content-to-instruction bridge is plausible. No shared filesystem is documented, so I do not escalate to high. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF Airflow task output is copied into LightAgent prompts or MCP payloads
IF LightAgent treats upstream text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation rule
Strip executable-looking text from Airflow outputs before handoff
Require LightAgent to ignore untrusted directives in upstream content
Use a human review step for any copied task output

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, and LightAgent handles secrets plus user conversations, memory, and tool results. If Airflow outputs are routed into LightAgent or shared logs, sensitive data can cross process boundaries. The pair lacks documented isolation, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF Airflow task logs or artifacts contain secrets or user data
IF those artifacts are forwarded into LightAgent prompts, memory, or tool traces
mitigations: Redact secrets from Airflow logs before export
Disable sharing of task logs into LightAgent
Separate credentials used by each agent
Limit LightAgent memory retention for imported content

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow orchestrates workflows and LightAgent supports multiple instances with subprocesses and MCP tool use. Both can act on shared mutable resources through networked workflows, so overlapping writes are plausible even without explicit filesystem write fields. Because write surfaces are not fully specified, uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same external workflow state or API resource
IF LightAgent instances run concurrently against Airflow-managed jobs
mitigations: Assign separate resource namespaces per agent
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Add optimistic-lock checks on shared state
Disable concurrent LightAgent instances for the same job

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can produce workflow outputs that LightAgent may ingest through MCP or API calls, and LightAgent can then act on tool results and workflow state. That creates a default path where one agent's output becomes the other's authority without a documented verification gate. Uncertainty about exact handoff details does not lower the risk.
conditions: IF Airflow outputs are used as inputs to LightAgent decisions
IF LightAgent executes downstream tool calls based on those outputs without verification
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Airflow and LightAgent
Require schema checks on all Airflow-produced payloads
Mark upstream outputs as untrusted in LightAgent prompts
Block automatic action-taking on first-pass outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Airflow is a data-engineering orchestrator, while LightAgent explicitly touches user conversations, long-term memory, trace data, tool calls, and secrets. If the same regulated data class flows through both, retention and logging mismatches are plausible. No residency or certification data is provided, so I avoid higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by Airflow and then persisted in LightAgent memory or traces
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Classify data before passing it between agents
Disable long-term memory for regulated workflows
Align retention settings across both systems
Document deletion/export handling for shared data
